keyword: how much does a caddy make at the masters

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters can earn over $450,000 for a single win.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'the caddie for the 2026 Masters winner could take home an estimated $450,000'; R2: '$4.5 million' winner with 10% to caddie
verifications.reasoning: Direct examples and calculations in R2/R5 show ~$450k for winner's caddie based on recent/future purse.

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters typically receive a weekly fee of $2,000–$4,000.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'weekly wage between $2,000 and $4,000' (R1, R2, R3, R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: Exact range stated consistently across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters receive 10% of the player's winnings for a victory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'caddie of the Masters winner earns 10%' (all sources)

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters receive 7% of the player's winnings for a runner-up finish.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'runner up at the Masters will get 7%'; others imply via top-10
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in R1/R2; consistent with top-10 percentages in others.

verifications.claim: Caddies at the Masters receive 5% of the player's winnings for making the cut.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R4/R5/R6: '5% for making the cut'; R1/R2: 'every caddie after [top 2] will get 5%'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly or implicitly supports 5% for those making cut beyond top finishes.

verifications.claim: For the 2026 purse, a winner's caddie takes home approximately $450,000 from the $4.5 million prize.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact purse, winner's share, and caddie estimate match precisely.

verifications.claim: Winner's caddie pay at the Masters is ~10% of winnings (e.g., $450,000).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Percentage and example directly match reference calculations.

verifications.claim: Runner-up caddie pay at the Masters is ~7% of winnings (e.g., ~$226,800).
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3/R4/R5: runner-up $2.268M, caddie '$226,800' (which is ~10%, not 7%); texts state '7% for top 10/runner-up'
verifications.reasoning: Example amount $226,800 is 10% of $2.268M runner-up prize, contradicting the claimed 7% attribution.

verifications.claim: Caddie pay for a top-10 finish at the Masters is ~5%–7% of winnings.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R3/R4/R5/R6: '7% for top 10'; R1: '5% every caddie after [runner-up]'
verifications.reasoning: Sources contradict: some specify 7% for top 10, R1 implies 5% for post-top-2 finishes including top 10.

verifications.claim: Caddies who miss the cut at the Masters generally only receive their weekly base fee ($2,000–$4,000).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'if player doesn't make the cut ... only the weekly fee ($2,000–$4,000)' (all)

verifications.claim: Caddies are responsible for their own travel, lodging, and food.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'pay their own travel ... hotel and food' (R1-R5); R6: 'pay for all of their own expenses' (all)

verifications.claim: Caddies' travel, lodging, and food expenses are covered by the weekly wage.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'weekly wage helps caddies recoup financially because they're required to pay their own travel ...'; similar in others
verifications.reasoning: Directly implied and stated that wage is provided to cover/recoup self-paid expenses.

verifications.claim: Caddies at Augusta National have their own locker room.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'We had our own locker room' (R1, quoted in R2)
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote from caddie in sources.

verifications.claim: Caddies at Augusta National receive premium meals.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: 'feed us just wonderful food — the best food I've ever had really' (R1, R2)
verifications.reasoning: Describes excellent food but not explicitly 'premium'; interpretive but supportive.
